newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO end Hebron University standoff -PLO.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO end Hebron University standoff -PLO.

text.p: A PLO negotiator said a confrontation over learning centres closed last March ended on Monday with Israel agreeing to let a polytechnic institute reopen and to discuss arrangements for classes in Hebron University.
The Israeli army had no immediate confirmation.
The standoff had developed when Israeli army jeeps surrounded Hebron University campus after about 300 students and faculty members broke into the compound vowing to resume studies, witnesses said.

"The standoff has been resolved with an agreement to reopen the Polytechnic Institute and then to sit down to work out an arrangement for opening the university," Musallam al-Daoudi, a PLO negotiator told Reuters.
He said Israeli officials "at the highest level" promised to let the university reopen, with talks of arrangements within three days.
Daoudi said Israeli soldiers were to begin withdrawing soon and the students would leave the campus shortly afterwards.

Palestinians said the students, expecting Israeli soldiers to storm the campus, had brought crates of onions to neutralise the effects of tear gas. At one point, negotiations were close to breaking down and Israeli troops took positions around the campus.
Israel closed Hebron University and the Polytechnic Institute, a two-year technical college on a separate campus, in March during a wave of Moslem suicide bombings in Israel that killed 59 people.

The closure kept more than 1,500 university students and about 1,000 polytechnic students out of class. Hebron University organised registration in October near the campus but students were not able to study.
"It is our right to study at our own university," said student Ahmed Abu Snaineh.
"Yigal Amir killed the prime minister of Israel and they did not close his university," he said, referring to the Jewish law student who shot dead Yitzhak Rabin last year.
Hebron is the last of seven West Bank cities that Israel agreed to hand over to PLO administration under a self-rule deal signed last year.
But the partial withdrawal from Hebron has been delayed by Israeli demands for better security for about 400 militant Jewish settlers who live or study in Hebron amid more than 100,000 Palestinians.

Talks between Israel and the PLO, with U.S. and Egyptian mediation, have failed so far to bring the two sides closer to implementing the Hebron redeployment deal signed by Israel's previous government more than a year ago.
